name: The Mechanical Butterfly Conservatory
description: A Victorian glasshouse filled with clockwork butterflies whose wings are made of watch parts, sheet metal, and mica. They feed on nectar from gear-flowers, their flight winding mainsprings that power the conservatory's perpetual motion.
prompt: Interior of a massive Victorian iron-and-glass conservatory. Thousands of mechanical butterflies: wings of brass gears, copper filigree, mica sheets, watch mainsprings, enamel details. They perch on gear-flowers (petals of meshed cogs, stamens of watch hands) drinking golden oil-nectar. Their flight winds invisible mainsprings powering the building's slow rotation. Sunlight through glass creates prismatic reflections on metal wings. Some butterflies have transparent wing-cases revealing tiny tourbillons. Brass vines climb columns. Steam vents release scented oil mist. Warm golden-hour lighting, dust motes, intricate macro details on each unique butterfly. Steampunk bioluminescence.
caption: They don't eat nectar -- they drink time. ⚙️🦋 Each wingbeat winds the conservatory's heart. A thousand tiny tourbillons catching sun. What happens when they all take flight at once?
